newsitem.title: THAILAND: Singapore's DBS seen taking 60 pct in Thai firm.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's DBS seen taking 60 pct in Thai firm.

text.p: The Development Bank of Singapore is set to take a 60 percent stake in Sri Dhana Finance and Securities Plc, a senior central bank official said on Thursday.
The proposed deal follows Thailand's recent easing of rules on foreign equity participation and the central bank approved the proposal in principle, he said.
Both parties were finalising the deal.
"It is a welcome development which is in line with the central bank's policy," he said.
Sri Dhana. in which DBS now holds about 10 percent stake, was one of 10 finance companies ordered by the Bank of Thailand in March to increase its capital.
But it was not included in the list of 16 ailing finance companies that the authorities suspended recently and ordered to merge or consolidate with stronger ones.

Thai financial authorities, in a move to attract foreign inflows to avert a financial meltdown, had recently issued decrees allowing foreign investors to hold more than 25 percent stake in finance firms.
The central bank had sent a strong signal that it wanted the sector to consolidate through mergers and acquisitions and let the financially distressed ones go under.
